summary: What a page may call on window.SF. A public name keeps its meaning and is renamed or removed only through the change journal, as an attribute is; an internal one is the runtime's and may change in any release. tests/browser/public-js-api.browser.mjs holds the list against the runtime: every name the runtime puts on window.SF is here, and every public name and member the probe loads is there. A component's script API (SF.Modal, SF.Input, ...) arrives with its component and is listed with it. loaded_by says when a name exists: core -- as soon as core.js has run, before the next script on the page; core-loader -- when the Loader has started, at the window event sf-loader-init (core.js loads it); smart-base -- when the Smart base has loaded (SF.loadSmartBase(), or the first Smart element on the page); component/<name>, smart/<name> -- with that component. The probe takes the names at each of those moments (documentation trial 6, 2026-10-18: the Loader's names were listed under core).

globals.name: SF.Loader

globals.name: SF.workspace

The events sf-workspace-view {view} and sf-workspace-panel {open} fire on the element (docs/developer/workspace-layout.md).

globals.name: SF.EarlyPort
globals.summary: Ports declared on elements (a <script type="application/json" data-sf-port> island: port, version, url, capabilities, first {intent, payload}): Core sends the first call when it runs, before any component's code, and hands the element the port with connect-port when it is defined; the port's first matching call takes that answer (one request). register(id, adapter) is the page's port registry for an island without a url; start and take are the adoption contract for a product's own adapter (one early answer per port, taken once, matched by port, version, intent and canonical payload, younger than 10 s). docs/developer/early-port.md.

globals.name: SF.ready
globals.summary: The Loader's readiness (simai/ui-source#16), on window.SF as soon as core.js has run. A thenable: await SF.ready (or SF.ready.then) settles with window.SF exactly when the Loader sends sf-loader-init -- SF.Loader, SF.loadSmartBase and the other core-loader names are there by then -- and a script that asks later gets it already settled; it never rejects. One per page: created once on the shared global, kept by every later bundle (a second core.js included) and never replaced. Called as SF.ready(fn), it runs fn once the Loader is up and the document has been parsed, synchronously when both have happened. A script that runs before core.js queues a function with (window.SF_ON_READY = window.SF_ON_READY || []).push(fn); fn is called with window.SF at the same moment.
